name: Bridge the Gap
line: A module-based curriculum on land, water and air — five to sixteen sessions, plus exposure trips and action projects.
deck: Between a hundred and a hundred and fifty Delhi schools every year. Land, water, air, waste, climate change — and who gets left out of all five.

scale.note: The programme is planned against both ends of this range. It is published as a range because a single number would have to be one of them.

aims.h: A place in the year, not a visit
aims.p: Success is a slot on next year's timetable that nobody has to argue for. An assembly is far easier to get and it changes nothing.

aims.h: Be affordable in time as well as money
aims.p: The programme has to survive a school that can spare one period a fortnight, because that is most schools. A curriculum only the generous can take is a pilot.
The target is a class doing something in its own building without us. If we have to be in the room for it, we have built a performance.
What we want to leave behind is somebody on the staff who can run it next year. Here the exit is the objective rather than the risk.

how.p: Five sessions, or sixteen. On land, water and air. A school takes the depth it can actually timetable, which is why the range is that wide.

how.h: Two leadership journeys ran inside it
how.p: CineGreen and Ride the Van ran alongside the year-long curricula in 2019–20, across over two hundred schools.

activities.name: Exposure trips
activities.p: Exposure trips take the students to the thing the module was about — the river, the landfill, the ridge. A number is not a smell.

frame.alt: Children in beige school uniforms standing at the edge of a landfill mound, a rag-picker working the waste behind them

activities.name: Action projects
activities.p: Every module ends in an action project the students pick and run themselves, in their own school or their own street. It is the part teachers remember and the part that is hardest to count.

frame.alt: A group of children in maroon school uniforms, each holding up a sapling growing in a repurposed plastic cup

activities.name: Teacher training
activities.p: The curriculum comes with teacher training, because a programme that only works while we are in the room is a visit, not a curriculum.

who.p: The class is the unit. It runs in a school that gives us five sessions and in one that gives us sixteen.
Training comes with the curriculum, so the second audience is the person who has to stand up and teach land, water and air after we have gone.

who.h: Schools that want a year, and schools that want a fortnight
who.p: The module structure exists so that a school does not have to choose between all of it and none of it. Depth is a timetable decision and we let the timetable win.

who.h: Whoever gets left out of all five subjects
who.p: Land, water, air, waste, climate — and who carries the cost of each. Inclusive ecology is in the curriculum because a class that never asks who pays has not finished the module.

done.p: The outreach count: a hundred to a hundred and fifty Delhi schools a year since 2000. It counts children in a school the programme entered — a different and far larger population than the fifty thousand who sat the sessions.

done.h: A hundred to a hundred and fifty schools a year
done.p: That is the current annual reach in Delhi, and the figure the programme is planned against rather than the one it is advertised with.

done.h: Fifty thousand students in fifteen years
done.p: Over 250 schools across Delhi NCR and over 50,000 students, cumulative.
Bupa Foundation and Acuity Knowledge Partners fund it now. Sir Ratan Tata Trust, Nokia Siemens Networks, American Express, National Geographic and Adobe have funded it before.

holes.what: Four figures that used to sit on this page — twenty-five thousand children, eighty-five schools, twelve hundred mentors, twelve cities — are withdrawn. Not one of them could be traced to any record we hold, and they were captioned as verified by us.
holes.unlocks: Nothing. This one is closed by deletion, and it is written down so that nobody puts them back.

holes.what: The three million is a derivation, not a register: schools a year, times years, times the children in a school. The middle term — how many children a school has — is not written down anywhere we can cite, so the figure carries the method instead of a source document. That is also the difference between this figure and the twenty-five thousand withdrawn above: that one was captioned verified and had no method at all.
holes.unlocks: One year's roll from one school turns the multiplier from an assumption into a measurement, and the three million from a derivation into a count.

holes.what: CineGreen and Ride the Van are named in our own account of a year and described nowhere on earth.
holes.unlocks: Two paragraphs would put the best unused material in this section onto the page it belongs on.

holes.what: We count schools and we count students. We do not publish what changed in one school after the sixteenth session.
holes.unlocks: Follow-up from a single school, at any scale, moves this page from reach to effect — which is the only figure a parent actually wants.

statement.line: Five sessions, or sixteen. The school decides.
statement.under: The wide end is the point. The same material has to hold for a fortnight and for a year without quietly becoming two different programmes.
